title: page-reshuffle-proactive-rewrite-and-latency-aware-spill
text:
page-reshuffle-proactive-rewrite-and-latency-aware-spill

description:
Motivation: Reduce tail latency and memory fragmentation for KV cache under mixed workloads by introducing a lightweight page reshuffle pass that proactively rewrites cold fragments into contiguous pages and a latency-aware spill policy that prefers low-latency candidates during congestion. Scope: runtime cache manager changes, pager heuristics, a new page-reshuffle worker, unit and integration tests, and a telemetry metric set for reshuffle efficacy. Implementation summary: 1) Add PageReshuffleWorker that scans tenant-local fragment chains under low-load windows and issues compact-on-rewrite operations when contiguous free reservation is predicted; 2) Introduce a spillScore combining residencyAge, fragmentationEntropy, and recentRequestLatency to prefer spilling pages that minimize tail impact; 3) Modify pager to perform soft-reserve ahead of imminent spills to avoid mid-request KV cache misses; 4) Add adaptive backoff for continuous-batching interactions so reshuffle work yields to hot batching under latency pressure; 5) Expose metrics redwood.kv.reshuffle.{attempts,succeeded,reclaimed_bytes,avg_latency_ms} and extend tracing spans through the pager path. Tests and rollout: unit tests for scoring functions, integration test harness simulating tenant-mixed workloads, canary rollout opt-in flag redwood.kv.reshuffle.enabled=false by default, and perf lab A/B job showing 9-12% 95th percentile tail reduction on our mixed benchmark. See Linear ENG-4872 for evaluation plan and ENG-4981 for rollout checklist.

review_comments:
Ethan Cho: Can you clarify how soft-reserve differs from the existing reservation path; concerns about double allocation pressure; please add a microbenchmark
Sofia Ramirez: Soft-reserve is a lightweight token grab that does not commit memory until rewrite commit; added comments and microbenchmark results in the tests directory
Maya Patel: Request change: scoring weights should be configurable via scaler flags to tune per-tenant behavior; otherwise LGTM
Sofia Ramirez: Exposed spill scoring weights as runtime flags with safe defaults and added docs sections for tuning
Jonas Müller: Minor: prefer yield() over sleep_for in worker backoff to be scheduler-friendly; also add instrumentation to ensure we don't starve the hot path

author_replies:
Addressed: replaced sleep_for with cooperative yield and added a telemetry counter for worker yield events
Added runtime flags redwood.kv.spill.weight_age, redwood.kv.spill.weight_entropy, redwood.kv.spill.weight_latency and documentation in metrics_catalog.md

merge_notes:
Squash-merged after approvals; canary rollout gate set and feature flag off by default; post-merge job scheduled to run full perf workload across three instance types and will auto-promote if improvement stable after 48h

release_notes:
Introduce PageReshuffleWorker to proactively compact fragmented KV pages and a latency-aware spill policy to reduce 95th percentile tail latency; metrics added for monitoring reshuffle efficacy; feature off behind flag by default; tuning flags available for spill scoring weights

upgrade_instructions:
No DB schema changes; operators should monitor redwood.kv.reshuffle.succeeded and redwood.kv.reshuffle.avg_latency_ms after enabling feature flag; recommended to enable on a single dedicated node pool for 24h before broader rollout
